audit.whatIsWrong: Decisive Strike is discussed in eleven places as a silence and nothing else. The half of it that breaks this matchup for Ambessa is never mentioned anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Garen gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him. His next attack strikes a vital area of his foe, dealing bonus damage and silencing them.' Lacerate's slow — the tool the rest of the page keeps telling you to stick him with — is removed the instant he presses Q, on a flat 8s cooldown. So the slow is not a hold in this matchup, and the second dash of your chain has nothing to chase.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[2].d, report[5].t and whys[2] now state that Decisive Strike breaks every slow you own.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appears anywhere in this matchup, and the coverage report flags that none of Garen's abilities are named. Courage is 'damage reduction', Decisive Strike is 'his Q', Demacian Justice is 'his R'.
audit.why: Decisive Strike is 8s flat, Courage is 22s at rank 1 down to 12s, Judgment is 9s to 6s, and Demacian Justice is 120s at rank 1. Courage's 22s is the real all-in window and it is nearly two Lacerate cycles wide; Decisive Strike at 8s is short enough that you bait it rather than wait it out. Those two numbers are opposite instructions and the page gave neither.
audit.corrected: tldr, phases[1].why, phases[3].why, phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d and report[5].t now name the abilities and carry the numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2's 'why' claimed 'dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade', and Levels 4-5 was the generic 'lane-control window' template while the content layer calls that stage Ambessa's weakest.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund — no shield; Repudiation is her only shield. At 4-5 her Q is 14-11s and E 13-10s against an 8s Decisive Strike, and Perseverance regenerates a share of his total health every second he is not struck, so anything short of a committed trade is refunded.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why and phases[3].why now carry the real numbers and agree with the content layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was the generic 'the R lock isolates and finishes the chain — point it at the kill, not the tank', with no cooldown for Demacian Justice.
audit.why: Demacian Justice is 120s at rank 1 against Public Execution's 130s, and it executes on missing health with true damage. Chunking Garen to a third and disengaging is the single worst outcome in this lane, because that is exactly the health bar his ultimate is priced for.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Demacian Justice, its 120s cooldown and the execute logic alongside Courage's 22s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer for this matchup is written in the first person — 'the silence cancels whatever I'm mid-cast on', 'I farm with the outer edge of my Q', 'my weakest window'. Every other Ambessa matchup addresses the reader as you.
audit.why: It reads as someone else's match report rather than the reader's plan, and it is inconsistent with the rest of the champion's pages.
audit.corrected: early, late and whys[0], [1], [2], [3], [5] and [6] converted to second person while keeping their claims. whys[4] and mid were left in the first person on purpose — see notes.

edits.before: Dash his spin — weave combo, bait his W. Ambessa wins the Courage cooldown windows.
edits.after: Bait Decisive Strike, then combo him. Courage is 22s and that gap is your all-in.

edits.before: Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade. Only take the trade when Garen's Courage is down.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Courage's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your Q and E are at their longest here while Decisive Strike is 8s and Perseverance heals the chip — farm and wait for 6.

edits.before: The R lock isolates and finishes the chain — point it at the kill, not the tank. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Garen's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Demacian Justice is a 120s missing-health execute, so never leave him alive and low. Courage is 22s and blunts the burst you counted on.

edits.before: Garen owns the early game and it is all about his Q. The silence cancels whatever I'm mid-cast on and breaks my passive chain, so the empowered Maxim auto never fires — if I throw a Q cone or E spin into his face he just silences, lands the empowered strike, and walks off before my long cooldowns are back. I can't punish that yet: at Levels 1-3 I have one or two abilities, no full combo, and I'm energy-gated. So I farm with the outer edge of my Q, refuse extended trades I can't win, and try to bait his Q before I commit any cast.
edits.after: Garen owns the early game and it is all about Decisive Strike. The silence cancels whatever you are mid-cast on and breaks your passive chain, so the empowered Maxim auto never fires. Worse, that same Q breaks every slow on him, so Lacerate does not hold him for the follow-up. You cannot punish it yet: at Levels 1-3 you have one or two abilities, no full combo, and you are energy-gated. Farm with the outer edge of your Q, refuse extended trades you cannot win, and bait the 8s Decisive Strike before you commit any cast.

edits.before: It evens back out late, and it's honest — this is a skill lane from items on. My first-item Q1-into-Sundering-Slam chunks him, but his R is missing-HP true damage, so if I poke him low instead of bursting him dead he just executes me out of the all-in. His W damage reduction cuts my biggest combo and his true-damage R ignores my flat armor-pen. I win the fights where I commit R fully and finish before his execute threshold; he wins the ones where his regen and W let him survive to flip it. Respect the ult timer and don't let trades drag.
edits.after: It evens back out late, and honestly so: this is a skill lane from items on. Your first-item Q1-into-Sundering-Slam chunks him, but Demacian Justice is missing-HP true damage, so poking him low instead of bursting him dead just hands him the execute. Courage's damage reduction cuts your biggest combo and that true-damage ultimate ignores your flat armor pen entirely. You win the fights you commit R to and finish inside his execute threshold; he wins the ones where Perseverance and Courage let him survive to flip it. Respect the 120s ult timer and never let a trade drag.

notes: UNVERIFIED CLAIM LEFT IN PLACE, flag for the user: this matchup asserts four times that 'suppression ignores his tenacity' and that 'only the brief stun at the end of R is shortened by his W' — in whys[4], spikes[1].text, wants.you[0] and mid. Riot's Courage text does grant tenacity, but nothing in the data says how Ambessa's suppression interacts with it, and needsResearch.tenacityAffected on her kit file is empty, which the brief says means UNKNOWN rather than no. Per the instruction to leave unverifiable text alone I did not touch those four strings, which is also why whys[4] and mid are the only content fields still in the first person — rewriting them for voice would have made me the author of the tenacity claim. Ambessa's kit file flags grounding on Repudiation and grounding plus heal on Public Execution; Riot's descriptions contain none of that, so I made no such claim.
